It asserts only `Assert.assertEquals("Invalid password.", loginPage.getInputError())`. It does not assert: (1) that a LOGIN_ERROR event with INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS was emitted (other tests in the file do, e.g. lines 153-157), (2) that the attempted username is still the original user (getAttemptedUsername()), which is the key invariant this PR is about (the username must remain hidden and unchanged after a failed password during re-authentication), and (3) that the user context was not cleared (the subsequent passkey login at line 386 succeeds as the original user, which implicitly checks this, but only for the passkey path). The second failed-password attempt (line 404) is followed by a successful password login with the correct user's password (line 410) — but because the user context may have been cleared by the failed attempt (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler clears the user when clearUser is true; during re-authentication USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is set so clearUser is false, but this is exactly the behavior under test), the test does not verify that the username field remained correctly populated. Without asserting getAttemptedUsername() after the failed attempt, a regression that clears the user or empties the hidden username would only surface as a confusing downstream failure. The test should assert the attempted username and the error event after each failed password attempt.

findings.title: Unused import NoSuchElementException remains after the test assertion was changed to expect the element to be present
findings.body: PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey previously asserted `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))` (the old behavior where the webauthn form was absent after username submission). The PR changed both assertions (lines 200 and 211) to `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), Matchers.notNullValue())`, so NoSuchElementException is no longer referenced anywhere in the file. The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` (line 51) is now unused. This is a minor cleanliness issue (unused import) that will cause checkstyle/IDE warnings; it should be removed. Note that PasskeysUsernameFormTest still uses NoSuchElementException (line 202) so its import is still needed there.
